newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields end higher on softer crown.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields end higher on softer crown.

text.p: Swedish bond yields ended sharply higher on Friday, hurt by the crown which fell as foreign banks, U.S. funds and Swedish export companies were selling it.
Favourable U.S. data with a lower than expected PPI figure did not manage to turn market trends.
"The crown makes players refrain from stepping into the market, despite that it might look cheap," a trader said.
The six month T-bill climbed six basis points to 4.33 percent, while the ten year bond yield jumped 17 basis points to 7.08 percent.
The crown softened to 4.5700 against the mark from 4.5015 late on Thursday.
Dealers could not fully explain the heavy selling of crowns.
Focus is expected to remain on the crown and EMU.
The crown can even soften further, dealers said.
"I think it might stabilise at 4.5800 against the mark and at 7.80 to the dollar," a trader said.
The crown was trading at 7.7918 to the dollar late on Friday, up from 7.6341 a day earlier.
